cleared.result: cmp_journal.py found 0 normalised function hashes in common with op-reth for either binary (X Layer 98 storage-path functions, Celo 120), because the revm-context versions differ, so nothing carries over from the cycle 35 run. The source each binary names was read instead: celo-org/revm bd28f94 crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs (checkpoint records log, journal and selfdestruct lengths and increments depth; commit only decrements depth; checkpoint_revert truncates logs and replays journal entries in reverse; tstore journals the previous value only when it changes and removes on zero) and entry.rs (StorageChanged restores present_value to had_value; TransientStorageChange removes the key when had_value is zero and reinserts it otherwise). revm-context 18.0.3 from crates.io, which X Layer embeds, has the same checkpoint, commit, revert and tstore text apart from const qualifiers. This matches what src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 and src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-20 assume. The machine code of these routines was not run in rethj.py, so the 2,000 nested-frame sequences of the task were not run; see the lead.

leadResults.answer: On all six images (Celo celo-v1.0.10, X Layer v0.0.7.3-rc.1, reth-bsc v0.1.4 and hotfix, Arc v0.8.5 and v0.8.6) the 25 handlers, every EXP variant and analyze_legacy differ in text from op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and were run in the x86-64 model: 1,943,982 cases with 0 mismatches and 0 errors, the PoolManager jump analysis exact on each, no BMI2, ADX or AVX on those paths, and all planted arithmetic and jump analysis faults caught. 2,000 live vectors match on each of the four endpoints. The journal was read in source only; a follow-up lead is open.
